'''Philomena Efua Nyarko''' is a [[Ghana]]ian statistician and academic, and the former Government Statistician for Ghana, chief executive of the [[Ghana Statistical Service]] (GSS).<ref name="Citi_Oct_2015">{{cite news |title=Ghana makes improvement in key health areas |url=https://citifmonline.com/2015/10/ghana-makes-improvement-in-key-health-areas |access-date=15 July 2023 |work=Citi 97.3 FM |date=17 October 2015 |archive-date=15 July 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230715122819/https://citifmonline.com/2015/10/ghana-makes-improvement-in-key-health-areas/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="university">{{cite web |title=Dr. Philomena Efua Nyarko – Governing Council Member, President Nominee |url=https://ubids.edu.gh/about/university-council/dr-philomena-efua-nyarko |publisher=SD Dombo University of Business and Integrated Development Studies |access-date=15 July 2023 |archive-date=25 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240625065506/https://ubids.edu.gh/about/university-council/dr-philomena-efua-nyarko |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="ADRH">{{cite web |title=Dr. Philomena Nyarko |url=https://africadigitalrightshub.org/our-team/dr-philomena-nyarko |publisher=Africa Digital Rights Hub |access-date=15 July 2023}}</ref>

==Education==

Nyarko has a PhD in [[social statistics]], awarded by the [[University of Southampton]], United Kingdom.<ref name="university"/> She also studied at the [[University of Ghana]], and was awarded a graduate diploma in [[Population study|population studies]].<ref name="university"/>

==Career==

Nyarko started working for the Ghana Statistical Service in 1987.<ref name="university"/> During her time there, she worked on the Ghana Demographic and Health Survey 1995.<ref name="Ghana. Statistical Service 1993 p. ">{{cite book | author=Ghana. Statistical Service | title=Ghana Demographic and Health Survey | publisher=Ghana Statistical Service | year=1993 | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=0IZTTH7NUXgC | access-date=15 Jul 2023 | page=}}</ref> She left the organisation in 1996 and worked at the Navrongo Health Research Centre, leading the Demographic Surveillance System.<ref name="university"/><ref name="ADRH"/> She taught at the University of Ghana from 2001 to 2010, focusing on technical demography, basic statistics, and advanced quantitative analysis.<ref name="university"/><ref name="ADRH"/> During her time there she also worked for the [[Population Council]] on [[Sexual and reproductive health|reproductive health]].<ref name="university"/><ref name="ADRH"/>

Nyarko was appointed acting Government Statistician in 2010.<ref name="university"/><ref name="ADRH"/> She was appointed to the post permanently in 2013.<ref name="university"/><ref name="ADRH"/><ref name="GO_2016">{{cite news |title=Women's participation in politics is key to good governance |url=https://www.graphic.com.gh/news/general-news/women-s-participation-in-politics-is-key-to-good-governance.html |location=Accra, Ghana|access-date=15 July 2023 |date=19 July 2016|newspaper=[[Daily Graphic (Ghana)|Daily Graphic]]}}</ref><ref name="GW_2016">{{cite news |title=Gov't statistician Philomena Nyarko retires May 11 |url=https://www.ghanaweb.com/GhanaHomePage/business/Gov-t-statistician-Philomena-Nyarko-retires-May-11-430860 |access-date=15 July 2023 |work=GhanaWeb |date=14 April 2016}}</ref><ref name="MG_2016">{{cite news |last1=Abban |first1=Kuuku |title=Government Statistician denies being hounded out of office as she retires in May |url=https://www.modernghana.com/news/685856/government-statistician-denies-being-hounded-out-of-office-a.html |access-date=15 July 2023 |work=Modern Ghana |date=14 April 2016}}</ref> Her predecessor had been [[Grace Bediako]].<ref name="GW_2016"/> Nyarko remained in post until 2016.<ref name="university"/><ref name="ADRH"/><ref name="GW_2016"/>

As Government Statistician, she was responsible for the 2014 Ghana Demographic and Health Survey report.<ref name="Citi_Oct_2015"/> She also worked on the National Strategy for the Development of Statistics and the Strategic Plan for the Improvement of the [[Civil registration|Civil Registration]] and Vital Statistics System in Ghana.<ref name="university"/> She set up collaboration between the GSS and [[Accra Technical University]] to give students access to statistical training.<ref name="Citi_2016">{{cite news |title=Accra Polytechnic signs MOU with Statistical Service |url=https://citifmonline.com/2016/06/accra-polytechnic-signs-mou-with-statistical-service |access-date=15 July 2023 |work=Citi 97.3 FM |date=11 June 2016 |archive-date=15 July 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230715122736/https://citifmonline.com/2016/06/accra-polytechnic-signs-mou-with-statistical-service/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On leaving the Ghana Statistical Service, Nyarko worked as a consultant and was on the Expert Group of the Regional Report of the African [[Gender Development Index|Gender and Development Index]].<ref name="university"/><ref name="ADRH"/> She is also on the board of the African Digital Rights Hub, as vice-chair.<ref name="university"/><ref name="ADRH"/> She is on the board of the [[University for Development Studies]].<ref name="university"/> Nyarko is also working on the Second Phase of the Global Strategy to Improve Agricultural and Rural Statistics.<ref name="ADRH"/>

She has been listed by the ''[[Daily Graphic (Ghana)|Graphic]]'' as an example of women participating in governance in Ghana, and in the ''Junior Graphic'' as a successful female leader.<ref name="GO_2016"/><ref name="Kitcher 2014 p. 8">{{cite book | last=Kitcher | first=M. | title=Junior Graphic: Issue 691 June 4-10, 2014 | publisher=Graphic Communications Group Limited | year=2014 | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=PyTcfuWvdSIC&pg=PA8 | access-date=15 Jul 2023 | page=8}}</ref>

Nyarko has said that access to and take-up of [[Birth control|contraception]] should be improved in Ghana, or there will be adverse effects for the country's development.<ref name="GNA_2015">{{cite news |title=Ghana must improve contraceptive growth rates – Philomena Nyarko |url=https://newsghana.com.gh/ghana-must-improve-contraceptive-growth-rates-philomena-nyarko |access-date=15 July 2023 |work=Ghana News Agency |date=23 May 2015}}</ref> She has also argued for an increase in the [[Marriageable age|legal age of marriage]] in Ghana from 18 to 23, in order to decrease population growth and improve women's health.<ref name="BBC_News_2013">{{cite news |title=Ghana official calls for higher marriage age |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-23351274 |access-date=15 July 2023 |date=17 July 2013|work=BBC News}}</ref>

With extensive teaching and research expertise, Dr. Philomena Efua Nyarko has offered technical guidance and strategic leadership to numerous public and private sector organizations.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Affairs |first=UBIDS Corporate |title=Dr. Philomena Efua Nyarko |url=https://ubids.edu.gh/about/university-council/dr-philomena-efua-nyarko |access-date=2023-08-16 |website=SD Dombo Univ. of Business and Integrated Dev't Studies |language=en-US |archive-date=2024-06-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240625065506/https://ubids.edu.gh/about/university-council/dr-philomena-efua-nyarko |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Personal life==

Nyarko is married and lives in [[Kumasi]].<ref name="MNG_2021">{{cite news |title=Mrs Philomina Nyarko, wife of another prominent personality goes missing in Kumasi |url=https://www.mynewsgh.com/mrs-philomina-nyarko-wife-of-another-prominent-personality-goes-missing-in-kumasi/?expand_article=1 |access-date=15 July 2023 |work=MyNewsGh |date=24 November 2021}}</ref> In 2021 she was reported missing.<ref name="MNG_2021"/>

==Publications==

===Statistical reports===

* ''A Situation Analysis Study of Family Planning Service Delivery Points in Ghana'' (1994), with K. A. Twum-Baah, [[Pamela Wolf]] and Henry Odai, Accra: Ghana Statistical Service
* ''The Pattern of Poverty in Ghana, 1988-1992: A Study Based on the Ghana Living Standards Survey'' (1995), with Harold Coulombe, Andrew McKay, Moses Avooner-Williams et al., Accra: Ghana Statistical Service
* ''Ghana Statistical Yearbook'' (2010), Accra: Ghana Statistical Service
* ''2010 Population and Housing Census: Summary of Final Results'' (2012), Accra: Ghana Statistical Service.
* (ed) ''Integrated Business Establishment Survey: National Employment Report'' (2015), Accra: Ghana Statistical Service.

===Journal articles===

* "The effect of community nurses and health volunteers on child mortality: The Navrongo Community Health and Family Planning Project", with Brian Pence, James F. Phillips and Cornelius Debpuur, ''[[Scandinavian Journal of Public Health]]'', December 2007, Vol. 35 Issue 6, p599-608.
* "Is a woman's first pregnancy outcome related to her years of schooling? An assessment of women's adolescent pregnancy outcomes and subsequent educational attainment in Ghana", by [[Adriana Biney]] and Philomena Nyarko, ''[[Reproductive Health (journal)|Reproductive Health]]'' 10 March 2017, Vol. 14, p1-15.
* "Contemporary female migration in Ghana: Analyses of the 2000 and 2010 Censuses" (2018), with [[Samantha Lattof]], [[Ernestina Coast]] and [[Tiziana Leone]], ''[[Demographic Research (journal)|Demographic Research]] ''39: 1181–1226.
